हैं, उसमें राग हो जाता है और जिसको दुःख देनेवाला मानते हैं, उसमें द्वेष हो जाता है । अतः राग-द्वेष अपनी भूलसे
पैदा होते हैं, इसमें दूसरा कोई कारण नहीं है । राग-द्वेष होनेके कारण ही संसार भगवत्स्वरूप नहीं दीखता, प्रत्युत
जड़ और नाशवान् दीखता है । अगर राग-द्वेष न हों तो जड़ता है ही नहीं, प्रत्युत सब कुछ चिन्मय परमात्मा ही हैं—

अर्जुनके मूल प्रश्नमें आया ‘ज्यायसी' ( ३ । १ ) और यहाँ आया 'श्रेयान्'– दोनों शब्द एक ही हैं। इससे ऐसा मालूम
होता है कि भगवान्ने अर्जुनके प्रश्नका उत्तर मुख्यरूपसे इसी श्लोकमें दिया है।
english:
The supplementary meaning is that attachment and aversion arise due to considering someone else as the cause of happiness and sorrow. That is, attachment arises for the one who is considered to be the giver of happiness, and aversion arises for the one who is considered to be the giver of sorrow. Therefore, attachment and aversion are born out of one's own mistake, and there is no other reason for them. It is due to attachment and aversion that the world does not appear as the divine form, but rather as inert and perishable. If there were no attachment and aversion, there would be no inertness, and everything would be the all-conscious Supreme Self - 'vāsudevaḥ sarvam' (Gītā 7.19).

If any defect like attachment and aversion arises in the mind and intellect, one should not come under its control, i.e., one should not perform any prohibited action according to it. If one performs actions under its control, that defect will become strong. However, if one does not perform actions under its control, a sense of enthusiasm will arise. For example, if someone says something bitter to us, but we do not become angry, then there will be a sense of enthusiasm and joy within us that we have been spared. However, we should not consider this as our own strength, but rather as the grace of the Lord, that we have been spared due to His grace, otherwise we would have come under its control. In this way, when a seeker sees any defect, they should not come under its control and should not consider it as their own. If attachment and aversion were our own, then as long as we exist, attachment and aversion would also exist. However, it is everyone's experience that we continue to exist, but attachment and aversion do not always exist, rather they come and go. Attachment and aversion cannot arise in the self, which is in the form of existence. This is because our own nature is separate, and the nature of attachment and aversion is separate. One who has the knowledge of the coming and going of attachment and aversion is separate from them. Therefore, attachment and aversion are separate from us, and they are also separate from the mind, intellect, etc., in which they appear - 'manogatān' (Gītā 2.55).

The meaning of the words 'indriyasyendriyasyārthe rāgadveṣau vyavasthitau' is that one should not have attachment in both favorable and unfavorable circumstances, but rather make good use of them, i.e., serve others in favorable circumstances and renounce the desire for favorable circumstances in unfavorable ones. The meaning of the words 'tayorna vaśamāgacchet' is that one should not become happy or unhappy in favorable or unfavorable circumstances. Becoming happy or unhappy is attachment to the fruit, and the person who is attached to the fruit becomes bound - 'phale sakto nibadhyate' (Gītā 5.12).

The relationship is that one should not come under the control of attachment and aversion, and what should and should not be done in this regard will be answered by the Lord in the next verse.

śreyaṃ svadharmo viguṇaḥ paradharmaāt svanuṣṭhitāt |
svadharme nidhanaṃ śreyaḥ paradharmao bhayāvahaḥ || 35 ||

svanuṣṭhitāt = having been well performed
svadharmo = one's own duty
śreyaḥ = is better
= even if it has defects
vigūṇaḥ = having defects
paradharmāt = than another's duty
= than another's duty
paradharmo = another's duty
= even if it is well performed
svadharme = in one's own duty
nidhanaṃ = death
śreyaḥ = is better
paradharmo = another's duty
bhayāvahaḥ = is fearful

Explanation: It is better to perform one's own duty, even if it has defects and is difficult to perform, than to perform another's duty, even if it is easy to perform and has many good qualities. Death in one's own duty is better than performing another's duty, which is fearful. 

The word 'jyāyasi' in Arjuna's original question (3.1) and the word 'śreyaḥ' in this verse are the same. This suggests that the Lord has mainly answered Arjuna's question in this verse.
